representation_plans.learner_operation: Trace how an interpreted symbol changes an interaction and is reinforced or revised.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: State the participants, the symbol, each interpretation, and the resulting action in reading order without naming the best lens.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Locate the shared practices that create and stabilize a category.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: List the category, the groups using it, and the institutional practices that maintain it without selecting the lens.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Identify the actor, alternatives, expected rewards, expected costs, and selected option.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: List each available option with its expected benefit and expected cost without calculating or naming the preferred option.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Compare each exchange partner’s dependence and access to alternatives.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: State what each partner receives, gives, and could obtain elsewhere without naming which partner has more power.

demand_inventory.description: Select symbolic interactionism when the explanatory work occurs through interpretation and negotiated meaning in interaction.
Select social constructionism when shared definitions are created and stabilized by collective or institutional practices.
Predict the evidence each meaning lens would foreground while keeping cost-benefit lenses separate.
Select rational choice when one actor chooses among alternatives by expected benefits, costs, and constraints.
Select exchange theory when an ongoing relationship depends on reciprocal rewards, costs, and comparison with alternatives.
Predict greater exchange power for the less dependent partner with better alternatives.

changed_task_decision_points.decision_point: The near task asks whether meaning is negotiated during an encounter; the changed task asks whether a category is stabilized across rules and records. Carrying the encounter-level choice forward misses the institutional maintenance cue.
near_trace: Identify the outcome that needs explanation.
Locate repeated interpretation of a symbol during face-to-face exchanges.
Select the lens whose mechanism is negotiated meaning in interaction.
changed_trace: Identify the outcome that needs explanation.
Locate coordinated rules, records, and repeated public use that stabilize a category.
Select the lens whose mechanism is collective construction of shared reality.

changed_task_decision_points.decision_point: The near task asks how reciprocity sustains an ongoing relationship; the changed task asks how one actor selects a standalone alternative by expected payoff. Carrying the relationship ledger into the changed task invents a partner who is not present.
near_trace: Identify whether the outcome concerns an ongoing relationship.
Locate reciprocal rewards, costs, and dependence between partners.
Select the exchange lens and predict continued interaction when the relation remains rewarding.
changed_trace: Identify the actor and the available alternatives.
Compare the actor’s expected benefits, costs, and constraints for each option.
Select the rational-choice lens for the individual selection.
